topic.title: Neural Network Pruning and Sparse Subnetworks
topic.overview: Pruning removes weights, units, or entire experts while trying to retain a model’s useful behavior. The cluster includes optimization-based sparsification, methods that allocate sparsity across layers, and searches for small subnetworks that can train successfully. A recurring distinction is between making a model numerically sparse and producing a structure that actually reduces deployment cost.
topic.whyItMatters: Reducing stored parameters and computation can make capable models usable on limited hardware. Preserving accuracy requires accounting for interactions among components, since independently unimportant units may still contribute collectively.
topic.evolution: Early representatives address network and rule pruning in the 1990s. Later papers integrate pruning into training and examine lottery-ticket subnetworks. Recent work targets deployment-specific structures, including vision-language-action models and interacting experts in mixture-of-experts language models, with layerwise subset-selection guarantees in the provided 2026 evidence.
openQuestions: When does a pruning criterion predict real hardware speed rather than parameter count alone?
How can pruning preserve rare capabilities that average benchmark scores miss?

papers.tldr: Sparse-IFT uses sparsity to expand architectural choices and improve accuracy while maintaining the computation budget of dense models.

papers.title: Sparser, Better, Deeper, Stronger: Improving Static Sparse Training with Exact Orthogonal Initialization
papers.tldr: Exact Orthogonal Initialization improves static sparse training and enables highly sparse 1,000-layer networks without residual connections or normalization.

papers.title: Sparsest Models Elude Pruning: An Exposé of Pruning’s Current Capabilities
papers.tldr: A large synthetic study finds that current pruning methods fall well short of ideal sparse networks, even with favorable initialization and width.

papers.title: Accelerating Non-Maximum Suppression: A Graph Theory Perspective
papers.tldr: A graph-based analysis of non-maximum suppression yields substantial benchmark speedups with either small or no reported detection-accuracy loss.

papers.title: AlphaPruning: Using Heavy-Tailed Self Regularization Theory for Improved Layer-wise Pruning of Large Language Models
papers.tldr: AlphaPruning uses weight-matrix spectral shapes to allocate pruning across layers, reaching 80% sparsity in LLaMA-7B with reasonable perplexity.

papers.title: ALPS: Improved Optimization for Highly Sparse One-Shot Pruning for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: ALPS makes optimization-based one-shot pruning practical and reports stronger language-model performance at high sparsity.

papers.title: BMRS: Bayesian Model Reduction for Structured Pruning
papers.tldr: BMRS uses Bayesian model reduction to prune whole network components, with two variants offering different compression behavior.

papers.title: DEPrune: Depth-wise Separable Convolution Pruning for Maximizing GPU Parallelism
papers.tldr: DEPrune structures fine-grained convolution pruning for GPU execution, reporting up to 3.74-fold speedup while preserving the evaluated model's accuracy.

papers.title: DiP-GO: A Diffusion Pruner via Few-step Gradient Optimization
papers.tldr: DiP-GO learns which diffusion computations to remove, reporting a 4.4-fold SD-1.5 speedup without accuracy loss in its evaluation.

papers.title: Finding Transformer Circuits With Edge Pruning
papers.tldr: Edge Pruning efficiently discovers sparse transformer circuits by optimizing connections, enabling faithful circuit analysis in models as large as CodeLlama-13B.

papers.title: GDeR: Safeguarding Efficiency, Balancing, and Robustness via Prototypical Graph Pruning
papers.tldr: GDeR dynamically selects graph training subsets using prototypes, reducing training costs while improving results under imbalance and noise.

papers.title: How Sparse Can We Prune A Deep Network: A Fundamental Limit Perspective
papers.tldr: A geometric analysis links pruning thresholds to weight magnitude and loss sharpness, with predictions closely matching experiments.

papers.title: Layer-Adaptive State Pruning for Deep State Space Models
papers.tldr: LAST compares state importance across layers, pruning 33% of states on average in tested multi-input multi-output SSMs with 0.52% accuracy loss and no retraining.

papers.title: Navigating Extremes: Dynamic Sparsity in Large Output Spaces
papers.tldr: Dynamic sparse classifiers enable training with millions of labels when changes to representation learning address their convergence problems.

papers.title: S-STE: Continuous Pruning Function for Efficient 2:4 Sparse Pre-training
papers.tldr: S-STE uses continuous sparse projection and fixed rescaling to improve optimization and model quality during 2:4 sparse pretraining.

papers.title: S2HPruner: Soft-to-Hard Distillation Bridges the Discretization Gap in Pruning
papers.tldr: S2HPruner uses controlled soft-to-hard distillation during pruning to reduce discretization losses and deliver strong results without fine-tuning.

papers.title: SequentialAttention++ for Block Sparsification: Differentiable Pruning Meets Combinatorial Optimization
papers.tldr: SequentialAttention++ combines differentiable importance scoring with combinatorial optimization to improve structured neural-network pruning.

papers.title: Shaving Weights with Occam's Razor: Bayesian Sparsification for Neural Networks using the Marginal Likelihood
papers.tldr: SpaM uses Bayesian model selection to encourage prunable networks and reuses posterior information for inexpensive pruning.

papers.title: SlimGPT: Layer-wise Structured Pruning for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: SlimGPT combines efficient component selection with nonuniform layer pruning to compress language models while reducing accumulated performance loss.

papers.title: SlimSAM: 0.1% Data Makes Segment Anything Slim
papers.tldr: SlimSAM alternates pruning and distillation to approach SAM's performance with 1.4% of its parameters and 0.1% of its training data.

papers.title: Sparse maximal update parameterization: A holistic approach to sparse training dynamics
papers.tldr: SμPar stabilizes sparse training dynamics and transfers hyperparameters across model widths and sparsity levels, reducing tuning costs.

papers.title: SparseLLM: Towards Global Pruning of Pre-trained Language Models
papers.tldr: SparseLLM decomposes global language-model pruning into coordinated subproblems, improving performance especially at high sparsity.

papers.title: BAME: Block-Aware Mask Evolution for Efficient N:M Sparse Training
papers.tldr: BAME adapts structured sparse masks while keeping both forward and backward training computations sparse.

papers.title: Distilling the Knowledge in Data Pruning
papers.tldr: Teacher predictions improve training on pruned datasets and can make random subsets competitive with sophisticated selection methods.

papers.title: DLP: Dynamic Layerwise Pruning in Large Language Models
papers.tldr: DLP uses weights and input activations to assign layer-specific pruning rates, improving performance retention at high sparsity.

papers.title: Lightweight Dataset Pruning without Full Training via Example Difficulty and Prediction Uncertainty
papers.tldr: DUAL uses early example difficulty and prediction uncertainty to reduce dataset-pruning costs while preserving strong accuracy.

papers.title: Mixture of Experts Made Intrinsically Interpretable
papers.tldr: MoE-X builds sparsity into expert activations and routing to improve intrinsic interpretability while retaining competitive language-model performance.

papers.title: SAFE: Finding Sparse and Flat Minima to Improve Pruning
papers.tldr: SAFE jointly targets sparsity and flatness to produce pruned networks with improved generalization and resilience to noisy data.

papers.title: SlimLLM: Accurate Structured Pruning for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: SlimLLM combines whole-component importance scoring, layer-specific pruning, and linear-regression recovery to improve structured pruning on LLaMA benchmarks.

papers.title: Sparse Training from Random Initialization: Aligning Lottery Ticket Masks using Weight Symmetry
papers.tldr: Permuting lottery-ticket masks to align with new random initializations improves sparse-training generalization in the reported experiments.

papers.title: Brain network science modelling of sparse neural networks enables Transformers and LLMs to perform as fully connected
papers.tldr: Brain-inspired connection initialization and rewiring let sparse networks match or exceed fully connected models in the reported vision, translation, and language-modeling experiments.

papers.title: Computation and Memory-Efficient Model Compression with Gradient Reweighting
papers.tldr: Reweighting gradients from older pruned sub-models reduces compression overhead while delivering strong sparsity, speed, and model-quality results.

papers.title: DiEP: Adaptive Mixture-of-Experts Compression through Differentiable Expert Pruning
papers.tldr: DiEP learns layer-specific expert pruning rates, retaining around 92% of Mixtral 8×7B’s original performance with half its experts.

papers.title: DuoGPT: Training-free Dual Sparsity through Activation-aware Pruning in LLMs
papers.tldr: DuoGPT combines weight and activation sparsity with accuracy corrections and GPU optimization to improve the accuracy–speed tradeoff without training.

papers.title: Global Minimizers of $\ell^p$-Regularized Objectives Yield the Sparsest ReLU Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper proves that global minima of its ℓᵖ-based objective recover the sparsest interpolating single-hidden-layer ReLU networks.

papers.title: Layer as Puzzle Pieces: Compressing Large Language Models through Layer Concatenation
papers.tldr: CoMe compresses language models by merging important channels across adjacent layers and then transferring knowledge through hierarchical distillation.

papers.title: Lua-LLM: Learning Unstructured-Sparsity Allocation for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: Lua-LLM learns where to prune weights across and within layers, improving reported performance over existing pruning methods.

papers.title: PermLLM: Learnable Channel Permutation for N:M Sparse Large Language Models
papers.tldr: PermLLM learns channel reorderings through differentiable soft permutations to reduce errors from structured language-model pruning.

papers.title: ReplaceMe: Network Simplification via Depth Pruning and Transformer Block Linearization
papers.tldr: ReplaceMe approximates removed transformer blocks with mergeable linear mappings, enabling training-free depth pruning with strong performance retention at modest compression.

papers.title: Sign-In to the Lottery: Reparameterizing Sparse Training
papers.tldr: Sign-In provably induces parameter sign flips to improve sparse training, while leaving the full gap with dense-to-sparse training open.

papers.title: The Graphon Limit Hypothesis: Understanding Neural Network Pruning via Infinite Width Analysis
papers.tldr: A graphon-based infinite-width framework connects pruning-induced connectivity patterns with differences in sparse-network training dynamics.

papers.title: TSENOR: Highly-Efficient Algorithm for Finding Transposable N:M Sparse Masks
papers.tldr: TSENOR efficiently constructs transposable N:M pruning masks at billion-parameter scale, enabling flexible sparsity patterns with promising model-quality results.

papers.title: Týr-the-Pruner: Structural Pruning LLMs via Global Sparsity Distribution Optimization
papers.tldr: Týr-the-Pruner searches globally for layerwise sparsity allocations, retaining 97% of reported dense-model performance while pruning half of Llama-3.1-70B's parameters.

papers.title: A Robust Optimization Guided Pruning Framework for Vision and Large Language Models
papers.tldr: RobOP improves one-shot model pruning by incorporating uncertainty in calibration data and algorithmic updates into the optimization.

papers.title: Attribution-Guided and Coverage-Maximized Pruning for Structural MoE Compression
papers.tldr: Channel-level attribution guides MoE pruning, preserving useful information while substantially reducing memory alongside quantization.

papers.title: Deterministic Differentiable Structured Pruning for Large Language Models
papers.tldr: DDP learns deterministic pruning masks that reduce model cost while limiting performance loss and delivering measured inference speedups.

papers.title: Don’t Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference
papers.tldr: Carefully configured layer dropout reduces LLM training computation and enables faster inference with little or no accuracy loss in the evaluated settings.

papers.title: EcoVLA: Environment-Aware Adaptive Pruning with Interleaved Inference Orchestration for Vision-Language-Action Models
papers.tldr: EcoVLA adapts channel pruning to changing environments and schedules pruning alongside inference to accelerate robotic models with small reported success-rate losses.

papers.title: Effective Model Pruning : Measuring the Redundancy of Model Components
papers.tldr: Effective Model Pruning derives how much to prune from importance-score distributions and provides bounds on retained score mass and loss change.

papers.title: SCHUR-A*: Layer-wise Optimal Expert Pruning for MoEs via Schur-Complement Guided A* Search
papers.tldr: SCHUR-A* uses mathematically guided search to select optimal expert subsets within each layer while balancing reconstruction fidelity and memory savings.
